# blakstrip

> A private, in-browser PDF redactor that removes content instead of covering it. Everything runs locally, nothing is uploaded, and it verifies the result before you download.

blakstrip renders your PDF in the browser with pdf.js and rasterizes the pages you redact, so the underlying text and vectors on those pages are gone rather than sitting behind a black box. Before export it audits what is hiding in the file (author metadata and timestamps, XMP, annotations, form-field values, embedded JavaScript, attachments, EXIF/GPS in embedded images, optional-content layers) and strips what it can; after export it re-inspects the output and shows you exactly what is still recoverable, including anything it could not remove. A strict Content-Security-Policy (`connect-src 'none'`) blocks network egress from the page, with a matching response-header policy over the pdf.js worker that parses your file, and the app works fully offline as a PWA.

## Tools

- [Redact a PDF](https://blakstrip.com/pdf-redact): Drop a PDF, draw boxes or search a term and redact every instance, then export a cleaned file. Audits hidden data on load and verifies the output before download.

## About

- [Home](https://blakstrip.com/): What blakstrip is, and why removing content is different from covering it.

## Notes

- All processing is client-side. No files are uploaded, and no analytics are collected.
- Redacted pages are rasterized (their text becomes an image); untouched pages keep selectable text.
- Known limits: EXIF inside a photo is detected but not stripped, layer (optional-content) PDFs are not fully cleaned on copied pages, and encrypted PDFs are refused. All three are surfaced to the user rather than hidden.
- Built by sixra.dev (https://sixra.dev)
